title: Jonah and the Terminal Again
premise: Rafael Montrose, a clone decanted after the original's unsolved murder, inherits both her predecessor's investigation and a dying colony the two rival fleets have agreed to abandon. When the colony's children begin sharing one dream — of a woman who looks exactly like Rafael — she travels there and discovers the original was killed because she promised the colonists rescue that would never come. To keep the fleets from open war over the colony's last fuel cache, Rafael sustains her predecessor's lie while racing to evacuate the children. In the end she exposes the truth at the cost of her own standing, saves the children as the colony dies, and chooses the found family aboard the evacuation ship over either fleet.
about_author: Elodie Thackeray is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. She writes science fiction about people who keep talking into the dark anyway.

chapters.title: Decanted
chapters.summary: Rafael Montrose wakes in a cloning facility with another woman's memories and another woman's murder case. Her handler, Okafor, briefs her: the original died investigating the Meridian Colony's abandonment. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief for a self she never met.

chapters.title: The Case That Outlived Its Detective
chapters.summary: Rafael reviews the original's files aboard fleet station Corvus, finding coded letters to Meridian promising rescue that no fleet authorized. A rival admiral, Serrano, warns her to let the case die. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: dawning suspicion that duty and truth have diverged.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet Planet
chapters.summary: On Meridian, twelve-year-old Iyo describes the shared dream to her teacher Ama: a woman with Rafael's face standing in a field of ash. The adults dismiss it; the children do not. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: eerie hope in a settlement running out of everything.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Rafael learns the original's promise nearly triggered war between the Concord and the Verity fleets over Meridian's fuel cache. The ceasefire holds only if no one returns. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: the weight of inheriting a lie that keeps peace.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: The dream reaches every child on Meridian the same night, each seeing the same woman mouthing words they can't hear. Ama records their drawings and sends a desperate transmission toward Corvus. POV Ama. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Signal From the Dead
chapters.summary: Okafor intercepts Ama's transmission and brings it to Rafael, who recognizes her own face in the attached drawings. Against orders, she requests passage to Meridian. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: terror and compulsion — the dream seems to know her.

chapters.title: Descent Into Ash
chapters.summary: Rafael lands alone on Meridian and is met by silent children who call her by the original's name, Mara. The adults are hostile; Ama is cautiously curious. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition — being mourned by strangers.

chapters.title: What Mara Promised
chapters.summary: Ama shows Rafael Mara's letters and the colony's failing reactor. The children insist the dream-woman told them someone was coming. Rafael begins to suspect Mara's murder connects to the fuel cache. POV Ama. Emotional beat: guarded hope meeting honest despair.

chapters.title: The Cache Beneath
chapters.summary: Iyo leads Rafael to the sealed fuel depot Mara discovered — enough refined isotope to power either fleet for a decade. Rafael realizes why Mara had to die. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: cold clarity about the stakes.

chapters.title: Serrano's Shadow
chapters.summary: A Concord scout ship enters orbit unannounced; Admiral Serrano has tracked Rafael. She hides the children during its sweep and realizes the fleet intends to seize the cache, not rescue anyone. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution she serves.

chapters.title: The Second Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: A Verity vessel answers Ama's old transmission, claiming humanitarian intent but clearly scouting the same cache. The two ships circle Meridian like knives. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: the children sense war coming before the adults admit it.

chapters.title: Keeping the Lie Alive
chapters.summary: Rafael transmits as Mara, telling both fleets the cache is unstable and mined — buying time while she improvises an evacuation plan for forty-one colonists. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: exhilaration and guilt of deception done for love.

chapters.title: Mara's Ghost
chapters.summary: Digging into facility records, Rafael finds evidence the original was murdered by a Concord agent sent to bury the cache report. Grief becomes fury. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: the clone avenging the woman whose life she inherited.

chapters.title: The Children's Council
chapters.summary: The oldest children, led by Iyo, confront Rafael: they know she isn't the dream-woman, but they ask her to be what Mara couldn't — someone who stays until the last shuttle. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: found family forming out of mutual honesty.

chapters.title: Reactor Failure
chapters.summary: Meridian's reactor breaches containment; the settlement has weeks, not months. Rafael must accelerate the evacuation or lose everyone. Ama refuses to leave the elders who won't go. POV Ama. Emotional beat: heartbreak of triage.

chapters.title: The Fleets Close In
chapters.summary: Both fleets demand Rafael stand down and reveal the cache status. Her Mara-forgery frays under scrutiny from an officer who knew the original personally. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: the lie collapsing under its own weight.

chapters.title: Confession Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rather than let the fleets discover the truth piecemeal, Rafael broadcasts everything: Mara's murder, the cache, the abandonment order. Both fleets freeze, exposed. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation — truth as her last weapon.

chapters.title: Standoff Over Meridian
chapters.summary: The Concord and Verity ships arm weapons while civilian shuttles lift through the crossfire corridor. Rafael pilots the final shuttle carrying the children herself. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax, love outrunning duty.

chapters.title: The Field of Ash
chapters.summary: In the shared dream's final visitation, the children see Mara and Rafael together in the ash field; Mara releases them, and the dream ends forever. The colony goes dark behind them. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: mourning and release.

chapters.title: Court of Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Aboard the neutral station, Rafael faces a joint tribunal. Okafor testifies on her behalf; Serrano's role in Mara's murder surfaces publicly. The cache is placed under joint civilian trusteeship. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Nobody's Clone Now
chapters.summary: Offered reinstatement by the Concord, Rafael declines, choosing instead to stay with the Meridian orphans resettled on the station. Iyo asks her to stop being called Mara. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: choosing found family over institution.

chapters.title: Signals Still Answered
chapters.summary: Months later, Rafael works the station's communications desk, relaying between ships that rarely answer. One night, a signal comes from deep space — a child's voice asking if anyone remembers Meridian. She does. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
